title: One authoritative writer
rule: Every enabled mutation entry point delegates to the fact owner; a projection or renderer never becomes an alternate master.

title: Captured expected state
rule: An existing-object replacement uses the expected state captured with the original read, never a fresh stamp attached to an old body.

title: Aggregate coverage
rule: Every mutation of fields or children in a revision boundary advances that boundary atomically; irrelevant telemetry does not.

title: Coherent read
rule: A returned edit stamp describes all returned editable data from one coherent observation.

title: Atomic check and effect
rule: The required target predicate and business invariants are enforced at the actual owner write boundary, not only at an earlier preflight.

title: Identity and lifecycle
rule: Profile/data epoch, object lifetime and content state have distinct meanings; stale or imported history cannot authorize a new incarnation.

title: Authority fence
rule: Current actor/claim/source authority is enforced where the effect occurs, including late results from cancelled or superseded attempts.

title: Bound decision basis
rule: Governed proposals name the required owner-validated source facts and set-membership witnesses; a model cannot omit mandatory dependencies.

title: No blind semantic retry
rule: Refreshing a token does not repair a stale intention or approval; a material basis change requires reconsideration.

title: Exact approval
rule: Approval binds the actual proposed effect, relevant basis and permitted authority scope; materially changed proposals do not inherit it.

title: Commit knowledge
rule: Known rejection, known commit, committed warning and uncertain observation remain distinct through every adapter.

title: Operation identity
rule: A scoped operation identity has one semantic request and at most one owned committed effect; duplicate delivery resolves that effect.

title: Draft survival
rule: A conflict, read failure, stale callback or post-dispatch typing must not silently destroy the current draft or its validation lifetime.

title: Projection safety
rule: A delayed projection cannot replace a newer source state or revive a retired incarnation; durable requirements have durable recovery.

title: Bounded coordination
rule: No human wait, LLM inference, external network call or unbounded traversal occurs while a correctness transaction or business gate is held.

title: Complete lock participation
rule: All writers of a guarded fact participate in the same documented exclusion/serialization protocol; keys and lock-class ordering are explicit.

title: Safe cleanup
rule: A failed/cancelled path releases every owned gate/context; cleanup failure after a known commit does not relabel it as rejection.

title: No hidden bypass
rule: Missing stamps, unconverted callers, bulk SQL, imports or test setup do not silently bypass a protected ordinary-write contract.

title: Owner-preserving boundaries
rule: Contracts stay data-only; shared infrastructure knows mechanics, not module-specific content semantics or service-locator routing.

title: Honest external effects
rule: External delivery and compensation expose their actual idempotency/conditional-write guarantees and uncertainty; no universal exactly-once claim.

title: Evidence before closure
rule: Discovery counts, current source identities, real database races and required UI/platform lanes are explicit; skipped or unavailable proof is not passing.

title: Bounded retention and disclosure
rule: Receipt/basis/audit retention respects retry horizons and access control; logs never expose secrets or unauthorized conflict values.

title: No notification dependency
rule: Correct writes do not depend on receiving a UI/cache invalidation event.

title: No-op semantics
rule: Every command defines equality/normalization and no-op behavior; no-op checks cannot conceal a semantically stale approved proposal.

title: Compatibility cutover
rule: Protected writers and their active callers transition as a coherent perimeter; old binaries or restored authority cannot re-enable unsafe writes.
